response.sql:
WITH group_avg AS (
  SELECT ID, AVG(ANA) AS avg_ana
  FROM Examination
  WHERE ID IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ana) AS overall_mean
  FROM group_avg
)
SELECT g.ID AS patient_id,
       g.avg_ana AS average_ana,
       g.avg_ana - o.overall_mean AS excess_over_mean
FROM group_avg g
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE g.avg_ana > o.overall_mean
ORDER BY excess_over_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Records with a NULL Examination.ID are excluded before grouping. Within each group, AVG(ANA) ignores NULL ANA values, so a group whose ANA values are all NULL has no average and cannot exceed the mean.

The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-patient averages, as the request states. Each patient counts once regardless of how many examinations they have. Groups with a NULL average are skipped by AVG.

The 'missing values last' sort rule has no effect here, because groups with a NULL average or excess are removed by the WHERE filter. The ORDER BY is still descending on the excess, which places any NULL last in SQLite if one ever appeared.
